title: The typo fallback shows far misses, and whole folders when a word is in the scope's own path
problem: When no hit has every word's letters in order, and Allow typos is on, the engine keeps everything fff returned (crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:578-580). fff lets a word miss `(len/4).clamp(2, 6)` letters (fff-search-0.11.0/src/file_picker.rs:1113; neo_frizbee lib.rs:302-304 defines a typo as a letter missing from the needle), so a 3-letter word needs one of its letters present, a 4- to 7-letter word may miss two, and the letters may be spread across the whole path. For `bduget`, a file `debug-test.log` (d, u, g, e, t in order) is as much a 'near miss' as budget.txt, and both are listed, up to the result limit, with nothing highlighted because highlight returns nothing for non-subsequences (1720-1723). A second case needs no typo at all: fff matches the path inside the root, but `strict` tests the path inside the scope (571-575). Searching `catalog` inside ~/Documents/Catalog, where no file below has those letters, makes every file in the folder a fuzzy hit through the folder's own name; none is strict, so the fallback lists the whole folder as results in place of 'No Results'.
proposal: In Engine::search, when the fallback applies (typos on, no strict hit), keep a hit only if every word is a real near miss in the shown path (the scope- or root-relative path): some window of the lowercased path is within optimal-string-alignment distance k of the word, with k = 0 for words up to 3 letters, 1 for 4 to 7, 2 for 8 or more. Implement `fn near_miss(word: &str, text: &str, k: usize) -> bool` as approximate substring matching (Sellers' algorithm with the transposition case, about 25 lines, no dependency); it runs only in fallback mode on at most `fetch` hits. Reword the Allow typos row in docs/manual.md:997 to say what counts as a near miss.
original_test_plan: Engine tests: root with budget.txt and debug-test.log, typos on: the names for `bduget` == [budget.txt] (today both). Root with Catalog/a.txt and Catalog/b.txt, scope = root/Catalog: `catalog` returns no hits (today both files). The names for `xqz` are empty where files contain an x, q or z. Unit tests for near_miss: (bduget, budget.txt, 1) true; (bduget, debug-test.log, 1) false; (cat, cot.txt, 0) false.
original_risks: This is a policy choice: fewer fallback results, and a typo combined with fzf-style gaps (`prjatlz` for Project Atlas) no longer matches. The thresholds are the reviewer's suggestion and easy to tune. Plain Levenshtein would count the transposition in `bduget` as 2 edits and break typos_can_be_turned_off (engine.rs:2073-2074), hence optimal string alignment. Best done after strict-check-scope-relative, which makes the shown path root-relative. It narrows behaviour of the Allow typos switch added in the Unreleased section; it does not duplicate it.

verifier.claim_check:
Both described behaviours are real, and nothing else in the code already handles them. I read the code and simulated the matching rule in Python; cargo was not run.

**Far misses in the fallback**
- crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:578-580 only runs `raw.retain(strict)` when typos are off or some hit is strict. With typos on (the default, config.rs:375) and no strict hit, every fff hit is kept, reranked and truncated (581-587).
- fff's typo budget is `(len/4).clamp(2, 6)`, taken from the first word (fff-search-0.11.0/src/file_picker.rs:1106-1113; 1200 for folders). Later words get `min(budget, word length)` (score.rs:92).
- A typo is a needle letter left out: neo_frizbee-0.13.3/src/lib.rs:302-304 and prefilter/mod.rs:5-9. The reference oracle at prefilter/mod.rs:1055-1067 is LCS + max_typos >= needle length.
- There is no score cutoff: matcher/algo.rs:88-106 pushes every prefiltered haystack, and fff-search score.rs:704-885 maps every match.
- So a 3-letter word needs one of its letters anywhere in the path, and a 2-letter word matches everything. The candidate's "4 to 7 letters may miss two" is really 4 to 11.
- Simulated: `bduget` matches both `budget.txt` and `debug-test.log`, and neither is strict. `xqz` matches every path with an x, q or z, such as `notes.txt`.
- On this repo's 157 tracked files as a stand-in tree: `taxes` lists 101 files, `invoice` 19, `recieve` 48. `settigns` lists 26, of which 3 are the settings files.
- `highlight` returns nothing for these rows (engine.rs:1720-1723).

**Whole folder through the scope's own name**
- `search_root` appends `<scope_rel>/**` as a glob (engine.rs:623-652), but fff still fuzzy-matches the root-relative path.
- `strict` tests the path with `req.scope` stripped (569-577).
- `catalog` scoped to root/Catalog therefore matches every file through `Catalog/`. None is strict, so all are listed in place of "No Results" (src/finder/mod.rs:3246-3249).
- The same `Engine::search` serves `/v1/find` (src/server/mod.rs:407).

**Docs and tests**
- docs/manual.md:997 already promises "near misses", so narrowing fits the documented intent.
- No test pins far-miss output. tests/controls.rs:339-340 (scoped `budget`, expects empty) stays empty.
- engine.rs:2074 (`bduget` finds `budget.txt`) still holds, because a swap counts as one edit.

**What the candidate missed**
- Requiring a near miss for every word drops hits where one word is an in-order abbreviation. Simulated: `rpt bduget` no longer finds `report-budget.txt`, and `pa bduget` no longer finds `plans/annual/budget.txt`.
- `shown` is the absolute path when unscoped (engine.rs:573 `unwrap_or(&hit.path)`), so letters of the root's own path count. On Windows it is also absolute when scoped, because `req.scope` is not in fff's base spelling (engine.rs:87-96).
- docs/manual.md:356 says `taxexemptionc` finds `token/exemption/coding/TaxHandler.java`. That path does not have the letters in order (no `a` or `x` before `exemption`). It only shows through today's far-miss fallback, and after this change it never would.
verifier.implementation_notes:
All code changes are in crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs.

**1. Make `shown` trustworthy first**
- This is the sibling candidate strict-check-scope-relative; land it first.
- `shown` should be relative to the scope when scoped and to the root when unscoped, computed where fff's base spelling is known. In `search_root`, `base` and the base-spelled `scope` are at 619-621; store a lowercased `shown: String` on `RawHit`. App hits can use the lowercased display name.
- Keep it scope-relative for scoped searches. If the sibling makes it root-relative there, `catalog` inside `Catalog` becomes a strict match for every file, and the second case is not fixed by this change.
- Without this step, an unscoped `usre` under /home/user is a "near miss" for every file, and the scoped Catalog test fails on windows-latest.

**2. Split the condition at 578-580**
```rust
if !words.is_empty() {
    if !settings.typos || raw.iter().any(&strict) {
        raw.retain(strict);
    } else {
        raw.retain(|hit| {
            let shown = /* same string strict uses */;
            words.iter().all(|w| {
                is_subsequence(w, &shown) || near_miss(w, &shown, typo_budget(w))
            })
        });
    }
}
```
- The `is_subsequence ||` part is the correction to the proposal. A word that already matches in order (an fzf-style abbreviation, or any word of three letters or fewer) must still pass; only the misspelled word has to be a near miss.
- Skip the whole block when `words` is empty, as today.
- App hits are always strict by name, so they never reach the fallback.

**3. `typo_budget(word)`**
- By `chars().count()`: 0 for up to 3, 1 for 4 to 7, 2 for 8 or more.
- These are tunable. In my simulation, 2 edits at 8 letters lets `vacation` hit `actions.rs`; 4 to 8 giving 1 and 9 or more giving 2 is the stricter option.
- Six-letter words must keep at least 1 for engine.rs:2074.

**4. `near_miss(word, text, k)`**
- Sellers' approximate substring match over `Vec<char>`, with three columns: `before`, `prev`, `cur`.
- Start with `prev = 0..=m`. Set `cur[0] = 0` for each text letter (free start).
- `cur[i] = min(prev[i-1] + (word[i-1] != text[j]), prev[i] + 1, cur[i-1] + 1)`.
- Swap case: when `i > 1 && j > 0 && word[i-1] == text[j-1] && word[i-2] == text[j]`, also take `before[i-2] + 1`.
- Return true as soon as `cur[m] <= k`. Return false early when `m > text.len() + k`.
- Then rotate the columns: `swap(before, prev); swap(prev, cur)`.
- About 25 lines, no new dependency. It runs only in the fallback, on at most `fetch` hits per root (665-669).

**5. Leave alone**
- `rerank`, `highlight` (near-miss rows stay unhighlighted) and `Engine::list` (documented as fff's own order).
- `total_matched` is not shown anywhere (src/finder/bars.rs:361-372), so it can stay as is.

**6. Docs**
- docs/manual.md:997: say what a near miss is. One letter wrong, missing, extra, or swapped with its neighbour; two in words of eight letters or more; none in words of three or fewer. The word must be spelled together, not spread over the path.
- manual.md:360 and 1098: align the wording.
- manual.md:356: replace the `token/exemption/coding/TaxHandler.java` example with a path that really has the letters in order, such as `tax/exemption/coding/Handler.java`. Fix the fixture and comment at engine.rs:1993-1994 to match; the assertion at 2024 passes either way.
- CHANGELOG.md: add a bullet under Unreleased, Changed. The fallback itself shipped in earlier releases ("on by default, as before"), so this changes released behaviour.
- Optional: the `typos` doc comment at crates/fffinder-core/src/config.rs:352-354.

**Engine tests** in crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs `mod tests`, following `typos_can_be_turned_off` (2046-2081): a temp dir, `Engine::new(EngineOptions { roots: vec![dir.clone()], app_dirs: Vec::new(), db_dir: None, watch: false, search: Default::default() })`, `engine.wait_ready(Duration::from_secs(10))`, and a `names(query, scope)` closure over `engine.search(&SearchRequest { files_only: true, limit: 50, .. })`, sorted.

1. Pure unit test `near_misses`:
   - `near_miss("bduget", "budget.txt", 1)` is true.
   - `near_miss("bduget", "debug-test.log", 1)` is false.
   - `near_miss("cat", "cot.txt", 0)` is false.
   - True for a dropped letter (`buget`), an added one (`budgett`) and `("settigns", "src/settings.rs", 2)`.
   - False for `("xqz", "notes.txt", 0)`.
   - All of these were checked in a Python simulation of the recurrence.

2. `typo_fallback_keeps_near_misses`, on a root with `budget.txt`, `debug-test.log`, `notes.txt`, `plans/report-budget.txt`, `Catalog/a.txt` and `Catalog/b.txt`:
   - `bduget` returns `budget.txt` and `report-budget.txt`. Today it also returns `debug-test.log`.
   - `xqz` returns nothing. Today it returns every `.txt`.
   - `rpt bduget` returns `report-budget.txt`. This guards the `is_subsequence ||` correction.
   - `catalog` with `scope: Some(dir.join("Catalog"))` returns nothing. Today it returns both files.
   - With `settings.typos = false`, all of the above return nothing.

3. Keep `typos_can_be_turned_off` unchanged.

**Portability.** CI runs macOS, Ubuntu and Windows (.github/workflows/ci.yml).
- Until `shown` is root-relative, unscoped tests see the temp folder's own letters. On macOS a `/var/folders/<random>` path with `b` before `d` makes `bduget` strict for both files. Pass `scope: Some(dir.clone())` in these tests, or land the sibling first.
- The scoped Catalog assertion needs `shown` computed against fff's base spelling. On windows-latest, `RUNNER~1` versus `runneradmin` makes `strip_prefix` fail, and the absolute path contains `\catalog\`.

**Optional UI test** in tests/controls.rs beside `search_scope_button` (329-358), using `Fixture::new`, `Ui::open`, `ui.click("search-scope")`, `ui.update(|f, _, cx| f.set_query(.., true, cx))` and `ui.names()` from tests/common/mod.rs:
- `xqz` gives no rows. Today it gives `notes.txt` and `Project Atlas.txt`.
- `raodmap` gives `Roadmap.md`.
verifier.risks:
- **Policy change to released behaviour.** With Allow typos on, these no longer match:
  - a typo combined with gaps (`prjatlz` for Project Atlas);
  - two typos in a word of 4 to 7 letters;
  - any typo in a word of three letters or fewer (`teh`).
  The switch name and docs still hold, but the CHANGELOG needs a Changed entry.
- **Ordering with strict-check-scope-relative.** Both edit the same closure. If that change makes `shown` root-relative for scoped searches, the Catalog case becomes a strict match and that test must be dropped. If it is not done at all, the near-miss check still leaks through the root's absolute path when unscoped, and through the scope name on Windows.
- **Candidates come from fff's top `fetch` only** (2,000 per root by default). In a very large tree a real near miss could be crowded out by better-scored far misses, giving "No Results". This is unlikely, because contiguous matches score highest, and the same limit already applies to strict hits.
- **The documented `taxexemptionc` example stops working.** It only shows through the far-miss fallback today; the docs must change with the code.
- **Thresholds are a judgement call.** Two edits at 8 letters still admits some loose hits (`vacation` finds `actions.rs`).
- **Cost.** The check is O(word × path) per hit, in the fallback only. Long words return few fff hits, so the worst case stays in the low tens of milliseconds.
